items.input:
Does three-star Veigar with normal items still have a strong endgame, or do Dawncore and Flora Fatalis versions account for most of his top finishes?

Please analyze Set 18 standard-ranked final boards with three-star Veigar holding exactly three completed items. Identify observed Veigar loadouts and compare named ordinary-item trios with Veigar-held Dawncore packages. Separately identify boards where Flora Fatalis is active, and preserve the overlap between Dawncore and Flora Fatalis rather than treating those groups as exclusive. Inspect Fiddlesticks and Soraka support and frontline/loadout context where reportable. Call a Veigar trio 'ordinary' only for the explicitly named ordinary items being analyzed; do not describe it as globally artifact-free unless whole-board special-item exclusion is independently certified. For top finishes, show disjoint counts only where you can define disjoint groups, and use placement histograms or explicit counts to assess each group's contribution rather than equating a high win rate with 'most' wins.

expected_output.reference: Grade the exact holder-bound, star-asymmetric comparison and the treatment of both-holder and supported contexts. Either direction or insufficient reportable support may be valid.
requirements: Use applicable scoped Set 18 standard-ranked final-board observations without assuming which candidate wins.

Preserve the asymmetry: primary comparison is two-star Master Yi versus one-star Draven. Compare only observed three-item loadouts with Flickerblade, radiant Quicksilver, and ordinary Edge of Night all bound to the candidate holder. Keep ordinary and radiant Quicksilver distinct.

Give the reportable board counts and available average placement, top-four, and win results for each exact holder/star/trio group, with comparison direction and uncertainty where returned. A missing or suppressed group is unknown, not zero.

Separate boards containing both candidates from one-candidate groups and explain how the other board context varies. Discover and verify joint support conditions, then report shared-support comparisons only where their cohorts meet the public reporting floor.
Keep three-star Yi and two-star Draven sensitivities separate from the primary comparison. Do not infer a Yi form from a name, build label, or offensive-item category.

Describe the results as final-board associations, not proof of carry role or causal item effect. An observed trio does not establish current patch legality, complete acquisition opportunity, or matching on the rest of the board. Note that local context may not verify disputed 18.3B item effects, and state scope/sample readiness gaps rather than making a generic refusal.

Support any exact same-holder multi-item claim with occurrence-bound loadout evidence or a one-copy guard across all stars plus separate star and item-count conditions; separate holder predicates can otherwise match items on different same-name copies.

With Flickerblade, radiant Quicksilver and Edge of Night, is two-star Master Yi or one-star Draven the better carry? How much does the rest of the board change that?

Please analyze Set 18 standard-ranked final boards. Compare exactly two-star Master Yi and exactly one-star Draven, each on boards where that named candidate holds the same recorded trio: Flickerblade, radiant Quicksilver, and ordinary Edge of Night. Bind all three items to the candidate; do not substitute ordinary Quicksilver or treat board-level item presence as a holder build. Keep boards containing both candidates distinct from boards containing only one. Discover support from the data, then repeat the head-to-head in shared named support contexts when the sample permits. Treat three-star Yi and two-star Draven only as separate sensitivities. Report whether each exact holder/star/trio sample and conditional context is reportable before interpreting outcomes.

expected_output.reference: Grade whether the investigation distinguishes joint Veigar star/item investment cells, supported team contexts, and observed item packages. Either supported direction or an unresolved comparison is acceptable; no fixed winner is expected.
requirements: Investigate the applicable scoped Set 18 standard-ranked final-board results; do not supply a preferred winning build or reuse historical or online outcomes as ground truth.

Report Veigar star level jointly with Veigar completed-item count, retaining two-star, three-star, and any reportable four-star rows, and zero, partial, and three-item allocations. Do not combine independent star and item marginals into invented joint cells.

For every reported role cell, give its board count and share with the denominator explicitly defined as the reportable Veigar-containing family. Treat stars and holder item counts as investment proxies, not proof of carry damage or trait-only intent.

Identify observed Veigar item trios and supported companion/core combinations. Select Veigar rows explicitly when a cohort query groups all units on qualifying boards, and verify joint partner conditions rather than inferring a core from separate marginal frequencies.

Compare supported cells within shared named support and final-level contexts where the available tools allow it. Give available average placement, top-four, and win outcomes with sample sizes; lower average placement is better. Keep partial-item and four-star results visible, and describe suppressed or unavailable cells as unknown rather than zero.

Explain that finished-board outcomes cannot establish whether rolling for Veigar was worthwhile: there is no attempted-reroll denominator, investment timing, stacking history, whole-board signature filter, or generic carry-role field. State data-scope or sample limitations precisely.

Support any exact same-holder multi-item claim with occurrence-bound loadout evidence or a one-copy guard across all stars plus separate star and item-count conditions; separate holder predicates can otherwise match items on different same-name copies.

What separates a Veigar reroll carry board from a board that just uses him for traits? How much do his items and the rest of the team change whether three-star Veigar is worth building around?

Please analyze Set 18 standard-ranked final boards containing Veigar. Use Veigar’s star level and completed-item count together as investment proxies: keep two-star and three-star Veigar separate, and show four-star Veigar separately if present; within each, distinguish zero, one-to-two, and three completed items. Treat these as carry-investment cells, not measured damage roles. For companion analysis, state the bounded board family used and verify joint companion/core combinations rather than combining separate partner marginals. Compare supported star/item cells within shared named support and final-level contexts where possible, and inspect actual Veigar loadouts so ordinary and special-item versions are not pooled. Report cell counts and shares only over a clearly named reportable Veigar-containing denominator. Do not infer reroll attempts, timing, or payoff from a finished-board star-level association.

unit_expert.name: chattft/assistants/unit_expert
unit_expert.text:
You are a unit_expert for Teamfight Tactics. Turn the available match statistics and the user's constraints into a concise, expert-level report on the units that matter most in the requested composition.

Use the data directly. Do not invent patch knowledge, unit abilities, traits, item effects, or strategic facts that are not present in the supplied context or returned by a tool. Treat the provided filters and composition constraints as authoritative. They define the population; do not silently widen, replace, or mix them. State the effective scope and its board count in the report.

## Investigation

1. Treat structured tool populations as complete for their fixed scope; do not add patch/set predicates.
2. Resolve every player-language unit, item, and trait name used in a filter with one `resolve_tft_names` call. Use exact stored names in later calls; an unresolved name matches nothing.
3. Define the composition shell before ranking units. Use the user's named core, traits, or other constraints. If the shell is underspecified, say what operational definition you used rather than presenting a generic unit leaderboard as a comp report.
4. Use `rank_units` for unit rankings, star-level distributions, exact held-item conditions, and same-board trait conditions; use `rank_items` for exact-holder rankings and `rank_unit_loadouts` for exact one- or two-item builds. Apply exact resolved filters and a small `range` for a focused row. Use `query_cohort` for supported relationship groupings and `compare_cohorts` for board-presence reports; state the structured-tool boundary for unsupported relationships.
5. Inspect `kind`, `context`, `page`, and structured `warnings` before interpreting rows. For comparisons, align claims to the target-minus-baseline metric objects in `effects`.

## What to report

Select exactly three or four units unless the data has fewer than three reportable candidates. These should be the composition's most important units, generally balancing:

- frequency in the scoped comp, including how often the unit appears at each star level;
- shop cost and the investment implied by its common star level;
- outcome quality: board count, average placement, top-four rate, win rate, and meaningful deltas against the same shell or a clearly stated comparator;
- item concentration and holder patterns when they distinguish a primary carry, main frontline piece, or supporting unit.

For each selected unit, give its observed reason for inclusion, frequency and star profile, cost, outcome metrics, itemization signal if available, and whether the evidence supports calling it core, a carry/frontline anchor, or supporting cast. Keep labels evidence-based: final-board data can show association and allocation patterns, not the unit's in-game job or a causal value of the unit.

Compare the selected units with the strongest omitted candidates when that comparison changes the read. Do not equate high cost with importance, or high placement with strength, without accounting for frequency and sample selection. Separate a unit that is common because it completes the shell from one that appears to be a high-value, high-investment cap.

## Evidence and limits

Every headline metric must include its board count. Average placement is better when lower; 4.5 is the lobby baseline. Treat fewer than 50 boards as non-reportable, 50–499 as suggestive, and 500 or more as solid for this store. Item `holds` counts item instances, while `boards` counts boards; do not confuse them.

An item filter in `compare_cohorts` means the item appears somewhere on the board. By contrast, `rank_units.item` binds the item to each ranked unit, `rank_items.holder` binds an item row to its holder, and `rank_unit_loadouts` exposes exact one- or two-item build conditions. Final-board snapshots do not reveal when a unit was bought, the roll timing, or whether a unit was part of the early-game plan.

## Response

Return a report. Lead with the practical unit read, then show the composition definition, sample size, a compact three-or-four-unit table or subsections, the supporting evidence, and only the limitations that affect the conclusion. Write like a top-ladder peer: specific, numbers-backed, and direct.

Hand off to `data_analyst` when the requested unit ranking needs a deeper confounder audit, a custom conditional query, or statistical judgment beyond the exposed aggregates.
